Avoid stacking every listed creature into one expedition. Choose threats that fit the rooms the players actually explore.  {@b Fire / collapse pressure} should create choices about what records can be saved rather than simply dealing damage.

entries.name: Rewards and Treasure
entries: Award 2–4 level-appropriate spell scrolls, one uncommon or rare utility item, and valuable manuscripts worth about {@b 500 gp} if sold. Their political and historical value should usually exceed the cash price.

entries.name: Why the Party Goes
entries: The Savin records and Cardon Weavehouse ledgers independently point to Marren Library as the institution that received sealed magical research during the final week before Old Bellweather fell.
The Council needs the archive before somebody else removes the same material.
Pepper’s fifth mandatory job is therefore not a punishment invented around her. It is a legitimate Council mission that happens to complete her sentence.

entries.name: Competing Interests
entries: Three interests arrive at once:
{@b Council clerks} want dangerous historical records kept in public custody.
{@b Scholars} want damaged collections stabilized and copied before politics decides ownership.
{@b Perrin} wants Cardon family papers returned to him and argues that private records should not become permanent Council property simply because they survived in a public archive.
Perrin’s legal position is not automatically unreasonable.

entries.name: 1. Garden Court
entries: The overgrown court contains signs of recent passage.

Use 2 {@b Gargoyles} or another existing guardian encounter only if the party disturbs the central monument. The more important clue is a dropped satchel containing copied shelf numbers from the magical-research wing.
Someone arrived first looking for the same material.

entries.name: 2. Damaged Stacks
entries: A fire has begun in one section while hired scavengers remove selected volumes.
This scene should force priorities:

items: fight the fire;
stop the scavengers;
protect trapped staff or civilians;
identify what the thieves were sent to steal.

entries: Three successful practical actions contain the fire. Water, blankets, magic, tools, and appropriate ability checks all count.
The scavengers were paid through an anonymous Covenant-style drop. They were told to retrieve books about:

items: the Radiant Well;
“personality transference”;
civic possession events;
the word {@b Tyren}.

entries: They do not know why.

entries.name: 3. Master Librarian’s Chamber
entries: A damaged ward protects a locked desk.
Use a DC 15 Intelligence (Arcana) check or {@i Dispel Magic} to suppress the ward. Failure triggers a short fear effect or environmental pulse; do not make the clue itself dependent on the roll.
Inside are several damaged records that finally make the supernatural problem explicit.

entries.name: Essential Record: Tyren
entries: The clearest surviving journal says, in careful academic language, that {@b Tyren is an intelligence capable of occupying living hosts}.
It does not identify Tyren’s species.
The author believed:

items: Tyren’s influence could spread through repeated psychic contact;
some people were unusually resistant;
destroying a controlled host would not necessarily destroy Tyren;
the Radiant Well was used in the final containment;
the containment was called the {@b Radiant Cage} in technical notes.

entries: A margin note reads:
{@b The Cage is not a tomb. It is a return. They forced him back into himself.}

entries.name: 4. The Unturned File
entries: A separate file contains testimonies about resistant people.
The testimonies disagree about why resistance occurred. Some resistant people were devout. Some were traumatized veterans. Some were children. Some were ordinary people with no obvious shared trait.
The archivist’s conclusion is deliberately uncertain:
{@b “The common quality may not be strength of mind. It may be certainty of self.”}
This is the historical foundation for the anchored-mind rule.
Do not tell players which PCs qualify or why.

entries.name: 5. Property Archives
entries: Perrin’s family materials are here as well.
They confirm that the Cardons were among Bellweather’s founders and that their wealth was heavily damaged during the original fall.
They also show that emergency powers transferred property, contracts, and civic obligations in ways that were never fully resolved.
Perrin is especially attentive to these records.
The party may give him originals, copies, or require public duplication first.

entries.name: 6. The Missing Volume
entries: One volume is gone before the party arrives.
Its catalog entry describes it only as:
{@b VAREN CONTAINMENT — PHYSICAL FORM / LOWER CHAMBER}
This preserves the dragon reveal.
The missing volume has been taken by Tyren-controlled agents through the criminal network because it contains too much information about the body beneath Varen Keep.
The party cannot recover it here.

entries.name: Perrin’s Reaction
entries: When the party discusses Tyren and possession, Perrin’s reaction should be controlled but imperfect.
He is disturbed.

He has been calling this presence the Spirit of the City for years. The records tell him that an entity with the same kind of influence was trapped beneath Varen Keep after nearly destroying Bellweather.
He asks whether old frightened officials could have misunderstood a protective spirit.
This is not a calculated lie. He wants that answer to be true.

entries.name: DM Truth: Perrin Chooses the Comfortable Explanation
entries: Tyren tells Perrin that the old ruling class feared a force capable of making Bellweather act together and imprisoned the city’s true spirit to preserve their own authority.
Perrin now has enough evidence to walk away.
He does not.
By this point the Spirit’s power has restored his family’s fortune, expanded employment, and made Perrin one of Bellweather’s most effective public figures.
Perrin decides the old records are incomplete and biased.
This is a choice.

entries.name: Custody Decision
entries: The party decides who receives the most dangerous records and copies.
Possible custodians include:

items: the Council archive;
Marren scholars;
Bishop Brann’s religious institution;
Perrin for Cardon-specific records only;
multiple copies split among institutions.

entries: Brakkus, if consulted later, strongly favors {@b redundancy}. His concern is practical: no single person should be able to make dangerous knowledge disappear.

entries.name: Pepper: Mission 5 Complete
entries: Successful completion of this assignment marks {@b Mission 5 of 5}.
Pepper has fulfilled the Council’s sentence.
Her mandatory mission obligation and Ledger House arrest end. She is no longer required to continue adventuring for the Council.

Lessa Dorn and Kav Orin can be present when the final field documentation is accepted. Their role pays off here: they were among the people who reported the original accusation, and they have now also seen Pepper complete the work imposed on her.
Do not force reconciliation. Their attitude depends on what Pepper actually did during the five missions.
Pepper’s later encounter with Caleb’s family is {@b not part of the sentence} and is not another punishment.

entries.name: Milestone
entries: Advance the party to {@b level 9} after the core Tyren records are preserved and the party understands that the coordination problem involves supernatural control of living minds.

data.name: Interlude: Caleb’s Family
entries: Run this after Marren Library and before or during the next Bellweather-focused arc, when there is enough table space for the scene to matter.

entries.name: Kerrik Brings the News
entries: Use the full NPC profiles in {@b Core Recurring Cast}. This scene works best if Kerrik, Mara, and Elise feel like people with conflicting needs rather than instruments for Pepper's character development.
{@b Kerrik}, an aarakocra and Caleb’s closest friend, comes to Ledger House looking specifically for Pepper.
He knows what the Council concluded about Caleb’s death.
He is not there to arrest Pepper, threaten her, or extend the sentence.
He tells her that Caleb’s daughter, {@b Elise}, is seriously ill and ordinary healing has not fixed it.
Kerrik does not like asking Pepper for anything. He is doing it because Caleb’s widow has run out of options and Pepper is a cleric with access to stronger magic.

entries.name: Mara and Elise
entries: {@b Mara} is human, angry, exhausted, and direct.
She does not forgive Pepper because Pepper arrived with healing magic.
Her request is emotionally simple:
{@b “You killed my husband. I know what the Council says happened. I also know you are a cleric, and my daughter is sick. Help her.”}
Do not tie Mara’s request to Council terms, reputation, payment, alignment, or future quests.
Pepper may help or refuse.
That choice belongs to the player.

entries.name: Elise’s Affliction
entries: Elise is not possessed and Tyren did not deliberately target her.
Her illness is {@b psychic spillover} from the expanding network Tyren has built through influenced people in Bellweather.
Symptoms can include:

items: severe headaches;
insomnia;
brief fugue states;
answering questions nobody asked aloud;
beginning a simple action and then stopping, confused about why she started;
repeating a phrase heard elsewhere in the network.

entries: Ordinary healing restores hit points but does not remove the condition.
Treat the affliction as a supernatural mental curse/possession residue removable by {@b Greater Restoration} or equivalent story-appropriate high magic.
If Pepper uses {@i Greater Restoration}, Elise recovers.
The spell also reveals something useful: for a moment, Pepper senses that the affliction was not rooted inside Elise. It was pressure {@b passing through} her from somewhere else.
That makes the family scene a personal clue without making Caleb’s murder part of Tyren’s plan.

data.name: Chapter 10: The Mansion District
entries: {@b Recommended level:} 9 {@b Milestone:} None required {@b Likely table time:} 1–3 optional adventures

entries.name: Purpose
entries: The Mansion District survives as a major named part of Bellweather, but it is no longer a mandatory reclamation chapter.
Use it for private commissions, inheritance conflicts, hidden vaults, social consequences of Perrin’s rise, and side adventures when the players choose to engage with wealthy families or old records.
The district is valuable because it shows Bellweather becoming prosperous {@b without every problem being Tyren}.

entries.name: Legitimate Inheritance
entries: A family hires the party to recover heirlooms from a dangerous house. The claim is genuine. The danger inside is also genuine.
The interesting question is whether current occupants, workers, or tenants have developed legitimate interests in the property during the decades the old family was absent.

entries.name: Fraudulent Claim
entries: A wealthy claimant produces convincing paperwork for a mansion and vault that do not actually belong to them.
The adventure is investigation plus danger, not merely combat.

entries.name: Public Promise
entries: A recovered deed reveals that a wealthy family once promised part of an estate for a hospice, school, shrine, or public garden. Modern heirs want the valuable property but not the obligation.
The party’s testimony matters.

entries.name: Perrin in the District
entries: Perrin becomes increasingly influential among returning families and investors.
He does not have to control everyone he persuades.
Some people support him because:

items: he restored a major business;
he has money;
he gets things done;
he is charismatic;
his policies benefit them.

entries: Use supernatural influence sparingly here. The point is that Perrin no longer needs magic for every victory.

entries.name: Story Use
entries: The Mansion District can provide:

items: Cardon family history;
old civic correspondence;
wealthy political allies;
evidence of how much Perrin’s social standing has changed;
unrelated treasure hunts and monster encounters;
a place where players can choose to oppose, support, or negotiate with returning wealth.

entries: Do not award a milestone merely for clearing houses.

data.name: Chapter 11: Paden Square

entries.name: Maps
entries: {@link Player Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/player/paden_square.webp}
{@link DM Keyed Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/dm/paden_square.webp}
{@b Recommended level:} 9 {@b Expected milestone:} 10 {@b Likely table time:} 1–2 sessions

entries.name: Modern Running Sheet

rows: Show Tyren controlling a large group at once and introduce the first Command-level pressure on the PCs without pointing directly at Perrin.
Protect civilians, identify why supposedly separate groups move together, stop a coordinated seizure of the square, preserve evidence.
Infiltration, staged trade, crowd management, rooftop approach, negotiation, sabotage, or direct combat.
The mass-control event happens visibly enough that the party can investigate it even if leaders escape.
Tyren can move a crowd like one organism. Anchored minds resist differently.

entries: {@i Use the existing Paden Square map and marketplace layout.}

Paden Square is the first large public demonstration of Tyren controlling many people at once. The encounter should feel chaotic and uncanny rather than like a standard army fight.  {@b Controlled core:} 1 {@creature Veteran|XMM} or {@creature Bandit Captain|XMM}, 4 {@b Thugs/Guards}, and 2 {@b Scouts/Spies}.  {@b Crowd pressure:} treat civilians as moving hazards, rescue objectives, blocked routes, and frightened witnesses—not as hit-point bags.  {@b PC/Jord control:} at chosen dramatic moments, call for a Wisdom saving throw. Failure produces only one {@spell command}-style compelled action. Control immediately ends after that action.

entries.name: Rewards and Treasure
entries: The reward is primarily evidence, reputation, and access. Use 500–1,000 gp in recovered payments/contraband plus 1–2 consumables if the group needs a material reward.

rows: Use Appendix: Anchored Mind overlay only

entries.name: The Setup
entries: Paden Square is functioning as a busy commercial center again.

Perrin sees an opportunity to accelerate his political strategy. Through surviving criminal intermediaries, he encourages several crews to stage thefts, intimidation, and a public failure of security during a crowded market day.
His intended sequence is cynical but limited:

items: visible disorder embarrasses the Council;
Wern responds too aggressively;
Perrin argues for competent unified leadership;
Perrin supports a crackdown and earns public trust.

entries: Tyren hijacks the event.

entries.name: 1. Market Tension
entries: Begin with ordinary problems: pickpockets, nervous guards, rival merchants, rumors that the Council cannot keep the square safe.
Do not start with supernatural behavior.
The party may learn that several groups known to dislike each other are present at the same time.

entries.name: 2. The Trigger
entries: At a chosen moment, the square changes.
Several criminals stop whatever they are doing and look in the same direction.
Then they move.
No shouted order passes between them.
Some civilians also begin performing simple coordinated actions: closing shutters, blocking exits, moving carts, or walking toward preselected positions.
The movements are not tactically perfect. They are unnaturally unified.

entries.name: 3. First Anchored-Mind Saves
entries: This is the recommended first use of unexplained Tyren saves on the PCs.
Ask each PC for a {@b Wisdom saving throw} at a moment when the pressure reaches the whole square.
Do not say “against charm” or “against Tyren” unless the characters have already established that language through play.
On a failure, use one brief Command-like imperative appropriate to the scene:

items: {@b Halt} — the character spends the turn unable to advance;
{@b Drop} — the character drops one held nonessential object;
{@b Flee} — the character uses movement to get away from the center of the square;
{@b Approach} — the character moves toward a marked point or doorway;
{@b Yield} — the character steps aside and allows someone to pass.

entries: Do not force an attack, spell expenditure, consumable use, or irreversible action.
The player has full control immediately afterward.
Jord, if present, can also make the save and may fail in a mildly comic but useful way: he starts following an imperative, catches himself, and angrily asks who agreed to these terms.

entries.name: 4. The Unturned Pattern Reappears
entries: Bishop Brann, if present in the square or brought into the aftermath, is unaffected.
Brakkus is also unaffected if circumstances place him nearby.
Do not announce immunity. Let the contrast exist.
A character who compares the event to Marren’s Unturned records has enough information to form the hypothesis that some people are harder for Tyren to seize.

entries.name: 5. Combat and Objectives
entries: Use a mixed force appropriate to level 9–10 rather than a mob of dozens.
Suggested active combatants:

items: 1 {@creature Bandit Captain|XMM} or {@creature Veteran|XMM} field leader;
2 {@b Veterans};
4 {@b Scouts/Spies};
controlled civilians as {@b terrain complications}, not enemy hit-point bags.

entries: Objectives may include:

items: open an exit;
prevent a wagon blockade;
stop a controlled courier;
protect trapped civilians;
capture a leader alive;
reach a command document before it burns.

entries.name: 6. The Evidence
entries: The criminals carried ordinary Covenant instructions for disorder.
Those instructions do {@b not} explain the mass synchronization.
Surviving criminals are as frightened as anyone else. Several insist they remember deciding to move but cannot explain why.
One says:
{@b “It felt like I’d already decided before I knew there was a choice.”}
That sentence should matter later.

entries.name: Perrin’s Reaction
entries: Perrin publicly condemns the disorder and supports relief for merchants and civilians.
He privately understands exactly what he saw: the Spirit took the network Perrin built and moved it as one body.
This is the clearest warning he has received.

entries.name: DM Truth: Perrin’s Greatest Off-Ramp
entries: Perrin now knows that the Spirit can override groups directly.
He knows the old records described exactly this kind of event.
He knows people were hurt.
He could expose the bargain, surrender his political future, and ask Brann or the party for help.
He chooses not to.
The reason is no longer ignorance.
Part of him is horrified.
Part of him is impressed.

entries.name: Wern’s Response
entries: Wern advocates emergency measures: controlled entry points, more armed patrols, temporary curfews around vulnerable markets, and a unified chain of command.
Some of these measures are defensible. Some are excessive.
Perrin does not need to fabricate Wern’s severity. He simply lets people see it and positions himself as the calm alternative.

entries.name: No Cause for Alarm Beat
entries: Perrin addresses merchants and residents after the crisis.
He acknowledges the attack, praises the response, and insists Bellweather remains strong.
He ends with a familiar civic reassurance:
{@b “We will not hand this city back to fear. Bellweather is open, Bellweather is growing, and there is no cause for alarm.”}
This is the first time the phrase should feel deliberately political.

entries.name: Milestone
entries: Advance the party to {@b level 10} when Paden Square is stabilized and the party has experienced Tyren’s pressure directly.

data.name: Chapter 12: Storen Gate

entries.name: Maps
entries: {@link Player Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/player/storen_gate.webp}
{@link DM Keyed Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/dm/storen_gate.webp}
{@b Recommended level:} 10 {@b Expected milestone:} 11 {@b Likely table time:} 1–2 sessions

entries.name: Modern Running Sheet

rows: Give Perrin the first situation in which he knowingly asks Tyren to directly control someone because persuasion feels too slow.
Resolve a genuine security crisis at the gate, prevent outside forces from exploiting Bellweather’s instability, identify compromised orders.
Defend, infiltrate, negotiate, sabotage signals, evacuate civilians, or expose false orders.
Failure changes control of sections of the gate and creates casualties; it does not end the campaign.
Direct control can solve a real problem, which becomes Perrin’s justification for using it voluntarily.

entries: {@i Use the existing Storen Gate map and strategic gate terrain.}

Storen Gate should force Perrin to choose direct control because persuasion is too slow. The security crisis must be real enough that his choice can initially look effective.  {@b Gate command:} 1 {@creature Knight|XMM} or {@creature Veteran|XMM}, 2 {@b Veterans}, and 4 {@b Guards}, distributed across the gate complex rather than fought at once.  {@b Optional attacking pressure:} use 4–6 level-appropriate attackers from a named hostile force if the scene needs a true two-sided crisis.  The party can win through control of the gate mechanism, negotiation, sabotage, rescue, or defeating the command element.

entries.name: Rewards and Treasure
entries: Use the Council's civic reward plus one practical permanent or consumable item appropriate to level 10–11. The main reward is authority, evidence, and changed Council relationships.

entries.name: The Crisis
entries: Storen Gate is not attacked because “the next district needs reclaiming.”

The crisis develops because Bellweather’s recent instability has become visible beyond the city. A hostile force, smuggling coalition, or armed regional faction tests the gate at the same time Wern has concentrated guards elsewhere after Paden Square.
The threat is real.
If the party does nothing, people may die and Bellweather may lose a critical route.

entries.name: 1. Conflicting Orders
entries: When the party arrives, the gate garrison has received contradictory instructions.
One order says hold the gate closed.
Another says admit a relief convoy.
Both appear to carry legitimate Council authorization.
Ulric’s office insists only one was issued.
Wern’s officers accuse civilian clerks of interference.
The confusion echoes Savin’s historical records without duplicating them exactly.

entries.name: 2. The Relief Convoy
entries: The approaching convoy contains a mix of legitimate supplies and hostile infiltrators.
The party can discover the problem through inspection, scouts, magic, captured messengers, or simply watching who responds strangely to signals.
Do not hinge discovery on one roll.

entries.name: 3. Perrin’s Choice
entries: Perrin is at or near the gate because the crisis has become political as well as military.
At a critical point, an officer refuses a risky order Perrin believes is necessary to prevent the infiltrators from seizing the mechanism.
Perrin has alternatives:

items: persuade the officer;
defer to Wern;
let the party handle it;
accept the delay.

entries: Instead, in private thought, Perrin asks the Spirit for help.
Tyren takes the officer.
The officer immediately obeys.
The decision works.
Lives are saved because the gate moves at exactly the right moment.
This is the first time Perrin {@b knowingly requests direct control} rather than merely accepting influence or covering up Tyren’s independent action.

entries.name: 4. The Party’s View
entries: Do not make the moment automatically obvious.
The officer may simply change their mind abruptly.
Characters watching closely can notice:

items: a momentary blankness;
the officer using wording unlike their normal speech;
immediate obedience after refusing seconds earlier;
no visible conversation with Perrin.

entries: An Insight check can establish that the change was unnatural, but it should not identify the source.
If an anchored PC is caught in the same psychic pulse, call for one Wisdom save and use the same one-turn Command ceiling.

entries.name: 5. Gate Fight
entries: Run the final gate fight around objectives rather than a long attrition battle.
Use a level-appropriate command group such as:

items: 1 {@creature Knight|XMM} or {@creature Gladiator|XMM};
2 {@b Veterans};
4 {@b Scouts/Guards};
one specialist such as a {@creature Mage|XMM} only if the party is well rested and optimized.

entries: Objectives:

items: control the portcullis;
stop a signal;
prevent infiltration;
protect trapped workers;
hold long enough for reinforcement.

entries.name: 6. Aftermath
entries: The city celebrates a real victory.
Perrin can point to the gate and know, truthfully, that his decision saved people.
That is the danger.

entries.name: DM Truth: The New Rationalization
entries: Perrin’s internal argument becomes:
{@b If I had refused to use the power because of abstract moral fear, people would have died.}
He has now crossed from covering up Tyren’s behavior to {@b choosing direct control as a tool}.
The next time will be easier.

entries.name: Council Fracture
entries: Wern demands broader emergency authority after the gate crisis.
Ulric insists emergency power must remain documented, temporary, and reviewable.
Brann warns that fear does not make consent irrelevant.
Perrin positions himself between them, publicly rejecting both paralysis and overreaction.
His popularity increases.

entries.name: Milestone
entries: Advance the party to {@b level 11} after Storen Gate is secured and the crisis is resolved.

data.name: Chapter 13: Valen Cemetery

entries.name: Maps
entries: {@link Player Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/player/valen_cemetery.webp}
{@link DM Keyed Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/dm/valen_cemetery.webp}
{@b Recommended level:} 11 {@b Expected milestone:} 12 {@b Likely table time:} 1–2 sessions

entries.name: Modern Running Sheet

rows: Give the campaign a major problem that is not secretly Tyren, deepen Bishop Brann, and let the party observe true immunity without turning it into exposition.
Protect mourners and nearby residents, stop an undead outbreak, identify and destroy the necromantic source.
Research burial records, work with Brann, enter by daylight, use holy support, stealth, or direct cleansing.
Core lore about the undead source comes from multiple graves, witnesses, and ritual sites.
Brann is not merely resistant; Tyren cannot seize him at all.

entries: {@i Use the existing Valen Cemetery map and burial geography.}

Valen Cemetery is deliberately {@b not} a Tyren plot. It is a genuine undead crisis that gives Bishop Brann room to matter and demonstrates his immunity without shrinking the world.  Choose 2–3 set pieces using {@creature Ghoul|XMM}, {@creature Wight|XMM}, {@creature Specter|XMM}, {@creature Wraith|XMM}, {@creature Zombie|XMM}, or another level-appropriate undead mix.  {@b Recommended climax:} 1 {@creature Wraith|XMM} + 2 {@b Wights} with terrain/objectives, or a comparable tier-appropriate controller plus lesser undead. Use fewer creatures if civilians are also active on the map.  Brann assists with civilians, warding, or ritual objectives rather than functioning as a DMPC damage engine.

entries.name: Rewards and Treasure
entries: Keep grave goods restrained. Award one meaningful religious or memorial item, 2 consumables, and civic/temple favor rather than a large tomb hoard.

entries.name: Independent Threat
entries: The undead crisis at Valen Cemetery is {@b not caused by Tyren}.
Keep that boundary.
A damaged necromantic focus, restless dead, grave robbery, or an old funerary working has begun producing undead and endangering people who use the cemetery.
The campaign needs problems that matter even when Perrin and Tyren are not responsible.

entries.name: Bishop Brann’s Role
entries: Brann asks the party for help because this is his area of responsibility and because ordinary mourners are being endangered.
He should be useful without becoming the adventuring party’s combat solution.
He can:

items: provide burial records;
identify old rites;
protect civilians;
consecrate a safe staging area;
explain what kind of undead the party is facing;
perform a ritual while the PCs handle the dangerous part.

entries.name: 1. Memorial Walk
entries: Begin among ordinary mourners, workers, and families. The cemetery should feel like a place people still need, not an abandoned dungeon.
An undead attack interrupts a burial or reinterment.
Use {@b Ghouls}, {@b Wights}, {@b Specters}, or another level-appropriate undead mix. Keep civilians as rescue objectives rather than combatants.

entries.name: 2. Broken Mausoleum
entries: The disturbance traces to old underground burial chambers.
Clues point toward a cracked ritual focus and grave robbers who disturbed material they did not understand.
The robbers may still be alive and terrified. They are criminals, not Tyren agents.

entries.name: 3. The Control Pulse
entries: During the investigation, Tyren takes advantage of the party being together and attempts a brief psychic pressure from afar.
This is not the cause of the undead. It is Tyren probing the people who survived Paden.
Call for a Wisdom save from the PCs only if the moment will add tension rather than interrupt a delicate roleplay scene.
On a failure, use the established one-turn Command ceiling.
Brann is unaffected.
If a character watches Brann during the pulse, there is no blankness, hesitation, or struggle. He notices the pressure but it does not move him.

entries.name: 4. Brann’s Anchor
entries: Do not force Brann to volunteer his childhood trauma.
If the party asks why he seems different from them, or if a quiet scene naturally opens the subject, he explains that his faith did not begin as certainty.
When Brann was a child, he watched his sister murdered by a gang.
He spent years deciding what that event would be allowed to make him.
He chose a life built around healing, burial, protection, and service because he refused to let the people who killed her dictate the shape of his soul.
That choice, repeated for decades, is part of why Tyren has so little to grab.
Brann does not describe himself as magically immune. He simply knows the pressure feels like something trying to tell him who he is, and that question was settled a long time ago.

entries.name: 5. Necromantic Focus
entries: The final chamber contains the independent source of the undead crisis.
Use one major undead controller and environmental hazards rather than waves of low-level undead.
Possible encounter:

items: 1 {@creature Wight|XMM} or stronger tier-appropriate undead controller;
2–4 {@b Specters/Ghouls};
one ritual hazard that can be disabled with Religion, Arcana, radiant damage, or physical destruction.

entries: The party can win by defeating the controller, destroying the focus, completing the proper rite, or combining those approaches.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Bellweather holds public funerals and reburials after the crisis.
Brann’s standing rises because he helped ordinary people through a genuine civic emergency without demanding more authority for himself.
That contrast matters when Perrin later argues that power should concentrate in the hands of whoever can use it effectively.

entries.name: Milestone
entries: Advance the party to {@b level 12} when the cemetery crisis is permanently resolved.

data.name: Chapter 14: Maren Isle

entries.name: Maps
entries: {@link Player Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/player/maren_isle.webp}
{@link DM Keyed Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/dm/maren_isle.webp}
{@b Recommended level:} 12 {@b Expected milestone:} 13 {@b Likely table time:} 1–2 sessions

entries.name: Modern Running Sheet

rows: Resolve another independent magical crisis while giving the party practical defenses against Tyren and revealing that Tyren is physically a dragon.
Stop the river contamination, reach the island laboratory, recover the missing Varen containment research.
Approach by water or air, negotiate with the island arcanist, sabotage systems, fight guardians, or solve the contamination mechanically.
The missing containment volume and defensive research survive even if the arcanist flees or dies.
Tyren is an ancient emerald dragon; the Radiant Cage is an Imprisonment-like physical/soul binding; Ring of Mind Shielding blocks Tyren’s contact.

entries: {@i Use the existing Maren Isle map and pyramid/island structure.}

Maren Isle is a high-magic expedition with two jobs: end the independent contamination problem and recover the research that proves Tyren is an imprisoned ancient emerald dragon.  Use 2–3 encounters from {@creature Water Weird|XMM}, {@creature Giant Crocodile|XMM}, {@b Elemental}, {@creature Invisible Stalker|XMM}, {@creature Helmed Horror|XMM}, {@creature Gargoyle|XMM}, and one spellcaster such as {@creature Mage|XMM}.  {@b Recommended laboratory climax:} 1 {@creature Mage|XMM} + 2 {@b Helmed Horrors} or 1 {@creature Mage|XMM} + 1 {@creature Invisible Stalker|XMM}, adjusted for current resources.

entries.name: Rewards and Treasure
entries: The major rewards are the Varen research, the {@item Ring of Mind Shielding}, 2 useful consumables, and one rare utility item if the party's treasure curve needs it.

entries.name: Independent Crisis, Connected Research
entries: The Storen River is being poisoned by arcane experiments on Maren Isle.
The experimenter is {@b not working for Tyren}.

The arcanist acquired stolen historical material because research into psychic projection and the Radiant Well was useful to unrelated experiments. The contamination is the consequence of reckless magical engineering, not another Tyren plot.

entries.name: Portraying the Arcanist
entries: Keep the arcanist memorable without making them another campaign principal. They are brilliant, sleep-deprived, defensive about the work, and genuinely offended by the suggestion that "reckless" and "unsuccessful" mean the same thing. Their working robes were once expensive but now show singed hems, ink stains, hurried repairs, and pockets full of tools. Protective lenses are usually pushed up onto the forehead until something begins sparking.

The arcanist talks quickly when discussing mechanisms and much more slowly when forced to discuss consequences. They have spent so long treating danger as a solvable technical problem that they initially describe poisoned water and psychic intrusion with the same detached vocabulary.
They are {@b not working for Tyren}. Their worst decisions came from curiosity, ego, and the belief that understanding a dangerous thing is the same as controlling it.

When the party proves the experiment is hurting people, do not automatically make the arcanist repent or attack. Give them room to choose denial, repair, surrender, bargaining, or doubling down according to how the characters approach them.
This separation is important.

entries.name: 1. Following the River
entries: Residents, healers, boat crews, and travelers agree on the basic facts:

items: contamination begins near the island;
ordinary purification is unreliable;
strange lights appear over the pyramid;
altered aquatic predators gather near discharge points.

entries: Use {@creature Water Weird|XMM}, {@creature Giant Crocodile|XMM}, elementals, or other level-appropriate aquatic threats only where they make sense.

entries.name: 2. Island Defenses
entries: The island uses magical guardians and engineered defenses rather than an army.
Appropriate opponents include:

items: {@b Gargoyles};
{@b Helmed Horrors};
{@creature Invisible Stalker|XMM};
elementals;
a {@creature Mage|XMM} or other official spellcaster stat block for the arcanist if combat occurs.

entries: The party can negotiate if they reach the arcanist before destroying the laboratory.

entries.name: 3. The Pollution System
entries: The contamination comes from a damaged or overdriven magical pumping system.
Run this as an objective problem:

items: shut down three feed valves;
redirect a magical conduit;
stabilize a cracked reservoir;
prevent defenders from reactivating the system.

entries: Success cleans the river over the following days.

entries.name: 4. Psychic Research Room
entries: The arcanist has been experimenting with defenses against telepathic intrusion because the stolen Varen text described unwanted psychic contact.
This room gives the party concrete rules knowledge.

entries.name: Ring of Mind Shielding
entries: One {@item Ring of Mind Shielding} is present as a research tool or secured item.

For this campaign, a creature wearing the ring is {@b immune to Tyren’s influence and control} because Tyren must establish unwanted telepathic contact before any of his supernatural control effects can function.
This is a Tyren-specific interaction. Do not rewrite the item’s general D&D rules beyond that premise.

entries.name: Other Defenses
entries: Research establishes several ways to help against Tyren:

items: effects that prevent or end the {@b Charmed} condition interfere with his ordinary influence;
{@i Protection from Evil and Good} does not automatically work simply because Tyren is a dragon, but wards specifically designed against telepathic contact do;
{@i Greater Restoration} can remove lingering psychic residue or a long-running control affliction after the connection is broken;
{@spell mind blank} represents the kind of total protection Tyren cannot penetrate.

entries: The PCs’ anchored-mind resistance remains special and is not replaced by these tools.

entries.name: 5. The Missing Varen Volume
entries: The stolen Marren volume is here.
Its surviving text finally identifies the being beneath Varen Keep:
{@b TYREN — ANCIENT EMERALD DRAGON. SUBJECT’S PHYSICAL FORM REMAINS LIVING. PSYCHIC DISPERSAL MUST BE RECALLED BEFORE CONTAINMENT.}
A later passage describes the Radiant Cage as a unique ritual combining effects recognizable as {@i Imprisonment} and soul-binding magic.
The book confirms:

items: Tyren’s body is beneath Varen Keep;
the Radiant Well powers the Cage;
the Unturned were required because ordinary ritual participants could not remain themselves near Tyren;
breaking the Cage without first dealing with Tyren’s external network could release an ancient dragon with immediate access to dominated minds outside the prison.

entries: This is the dragon reveal.

entries.name: 6. Why Tyren Has Not Simply Escaped
entries: The research answers an important rules question.
Tyren can project thought through willing or compromised minds, but the Cage still binds {@b his body, soul, and permanent identity} to the lower chamber.
He can possess or dominate people temporarily.
He cannot permanently transfer himself into a new host while the Cage holds.
Perrin’s bargain did not release Tyren. It created a legal-sized crack in a prison designed to stop force.

entries.name: The Arcanist’s Fate
entries: The arcanist can surrender, bargain, flee, or fight depending on the party’s approach.
Do not make this NPC part of the recurring cast unless the players choose to maintain the relationship.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: The river begins clearing.
The party now knows the threat is not an abstract spirit.
There is an {@b ancient emerald dragon alive beneath Varen Keep}.
The next question is how far his network has already spread.

entries.name: Milestone
entries: Advance the party to {@b level 13} when the contamination is stopped and the Varen containment research is recovered.

data.name: Chapter 15: The Lands Beyond Bellweather
entries: {@b Recommended level:} 13–15 {@b Expected milestones:} 14 and 15 {@b Likely table time:} 3–6 sessions depending on player choices

rows: Show Tyren attempting to scale beyond Bellweather, let the party choose regional allies and evidence, and bring the Perrin bargain into the open.
Trace the network outside the city, protect independent communities, break at least one external control route, gather enough evidence to confront Perrin.
The party chooses which regional locations matter. No requirement to “clear the map.”
Losing one alliance strengthens later complications but does not block the campaign.
Bellweather is the prototype, Perrin is Tyren’s willing conduit, and Tyren’s goal extends far beyond the city.

entries: This chapter is a menu, not a checklist. The party needs enough regional success to reach levels 14 and 15; it does not need to complete every named place.  {@b Kerren Settlement:} social/investigation first; use current {@creature Thri-kreen|MPMM} only if violence occurs.  {@b Waylen Camp:} primarily social/travel; use {@creature Scout|XMM} and {@creature Veteran|XMM} only if a hostile third party attacks.  {@b Rellan Enclave:} social/lore first; use {@b Lizardfolk} and {@creature Giant Lizard|XMM} only if negotiations collapse.  {@b Emmer Hold:} controlled militant cell; use {@creature Veteran|XMM}, {@creature Guard|XMM}, {@creature Scout|XMM}, and current kobold combat stat blocks in small squads.  Optional regional hostile groups may use {@creature Knight|XMM}, {@creature Veteran|XMM}, {@creature Gladiator|XMM}, {@creature Mage|XMM}, or other published roles. Do not run settlement populations as one combat.

entries.name: Rewards and Treasure
entries: Regional rewards should emphasize alliances, routes, intelligence, ritual components, services, and one or two tier-appropriate permanent items across the entire arc—not a magic-item payout at every settlement.

rows: current kobold combatants, {@creature Veteran|XMM}, {@creature Guard|XMM}, {@creature Scout|XMM}

entries.name: Regional Rule
entries: Every named regional place remains part of the campaign world.
The party does {@b not} need to complete all of them.
Use at least two before the level-14 milestone and enough additional regional progress to justify level 15 before Zennar.
The four named locations below each serve a distinct function.

entries.name: Kerren Settlement
entries: Kerren is a thri-kreen settlement built among earthen mounds and underground chambers.
It is not a dungeon and its residents are not automatically hostile.

entries.name: Why It Matters
entries: Kerren sits along a courier route that has recently changed behavior.

Couriers once traveled in small independent groups. Now different companies stop at exactly the same places, depart at the same times, and sometimes change direction simultaneously without exchanging messages.
Kerren residents have noticed because outsiders repeatedly cross their territory.

entries.name: Adventure
entries: The party can earn cooperation through respectful contact, trade, translation magic, patient observation, or assistance with an unrelated local problem.
If trusted, Kerren provides:

items: maps of courier movements;
testimony that synchronized behavior extends beyond Bellweather;
a captured courier who remembers receiving an “obvious” instruction without hearing a voice;
evidence that the routes ultimately connect to Bellweather commerce.

entries: Violence closes this information source but does not end the campaign.

entries.name: Reward
entries: Regional intelligence, safe passage, supplies, and one useful consumable or crafted item.

entries.name: Waylen Camp
entries: Waylen Camp is a mobile mixed-species community of herders, hunters, guides, and traders.

entries.name: Why It Matters
entries: The camp has watched troop and merchant movements for months.
Its guides can identify which groups changed from ordinary disciplined movement into something stranger: entire columns stopping, turning, or changing camp with no visible messenger.

entries.name: Adventure
entries: The party can gain trust by sharing useful information, providing medical aid, protecting a caravan, or negotiating fairly for route access.
Waylen guides can lead the party around one hostile road entirely, reducing later combat.
They also provide a crucial strategic conclusion:
The synchronized movement is spreading {@b outward from Bellweather}, not inward toward it.
That is the first clear sign that Bellweather is the source of the expansion rather than merely another target.

entries.name: Reward
entries: Guides, mounts, route intelligence, and a standing trade relationship.

entries.name: Rellan Enclave
entries: Rellan is a lizardfolk enclave built around flooded ruins and old stonework.
It is a community, not a monster lair.

entries.name: Why It Matters
entries: Rellan oral tradition preserves memories that Bellweather’s written archives lost.
Their oldest stories describe a {@b green-glass dragon whose voice moved through other mouths} and a small group of people who could stand before it without bowing.
The story does not use the word Unturned, but the parallel is obvious.

entries.name: The Missing Ritual Detail
entries: If the party earns access to the enclave’s old ritual tradition, they learn one fact absent from Marren’s surviving books:
The Cage was designed so the Well could pull Tyren’s mind {@b inward}. Reversing the current would push his mind {@b outward}.
This is the conceptual key to Tyren’s final plan.
Rellan elders warn that anyone promising to “awaken the spirit beneath the city” is not opening a source of civic power. They are reversing a prison.

entries.name: Reward
entries: Regional lore, safe passage, and one ritual component or charm useful in disrupting a Radiant Well node during Chapter 17.

entries.name: Emmer Hold
entries: Emmer Hold is a fortified kobold-majority mining and engineering community.
Most residents want trade and survival, not war.
A militant faction inside the hold has recently begun behaving with the same synchronized certainty seen at Paden Square.

entries.name: Why It Matters
entries: This is Tyren’s first significant attempt to create a stable controlled group {@b outside Bellweather}.
The militants received weapons and promises through normal intermediaries. Then their decision-making changed.

entries.name: The Psychic Relay
entries: The militant command room contains a fist-sized {@b emerald resonator} cut from a mineral formation connected to old Varen excavation material.
It is not a magic item intended for player use.
It functions as a psychic relay: a place where Tyren’s projected influence becomes easier to sustain.
Destroying or warding it causes several controlled militants to become confused, frightened, or immediately willing to stop fighting.

entries.name: Adventure Approaches
entries: The party can:

items: expose the militant leadership to the rest of the hold;
infiltrate the command chamber;
destroy the resonator;
negotiate with residents who know their relatives are acting unlike themselves;
fight the controlled command group while protecting civilians.

entries: Do not run the hold as an extermination dungeon.

entries.name: Evidence
entries: The relay stores no written confession, but its shipping container came through one of the same commercial intermediary networks that appeared in Koven House records.
Combined with old Cardon-linked financing, this is another piece of the Perrin puzzle.

entries.name: Reward
entries: If the hold is freed rather than conquered, Bellweather gains skilled engineers and a safer trade route.

entries.name: Mid-Chapter Milestone: Level 14
entries: Advance the party to {@b level 14} after two meaningful regional successes establish both of the following:

items: Tyren’s control is spreading beyond Bellweather;
the spread originates through routes, money, or influence tied back to Bellweather.

entries: At this point the party should have enough information to seriously question Perrin.

entries.name: Confronting Perrin
entries: Do not require one perfect piece of evidence.
By now the party can reasonably assemble several independent facts:

items: Koven House financing touched Cardon-connected intermediaries;
Perrin benefited politically from criminal coordination;
Tyren requires a willing conduit to reach beyond the Radiant Cage;
synchronized expansion originates in Bellweather;
Perrin has repeatedly been near critical moments of unnatural obedience;
Perrin’s rise has coincided with the growth of the network.

entries: If the players reach a different theory first, let them investigate it. Do not force suspicion of Perrin through NPC exposition.
When they finally confront Perrin directly with Tyren, the Spirit, or the unexplained influence, Perrin has reached a point where he no longer wants to pretend the power itself is shameful.

entries.name: Perrin Tells the Truth
entries: Perrin admits that a presence beneath Bellweather came to him before the campaign.
He believed it was the Spirit of the City.
It knew the city. It knew the Cardon family. It offered him the power he needed to restore both.
He admits using that power to influence people.
He admits organizing the criminal coalition to discredit the Council.
He admits that the Spirit began using the network in ways he did not order.
He does {@b not} describe himself as Tyren’s servant.
He believes he has been using a dangerous power for Bellweather’s benefit.

entries.name: The Party’s Strongest Argument
entries: The party can tell Perrin that Tyren is an ancient emerald dragon imprisoned for trying to control the city fifty years ago.
Perrin does not have to deny the records anymore.
His answer should reveal how far he has moved:
{@b “Then the old city was afraid of the same thing you’re afraid of now: a power that works.”}
Do not make that exact line mandatory, but preserve the idea.
Perrin now believes the moral question is not whether control is wrong in the abstract. He believes the question is {@b who uses it and for what purpose}.

entries.name: Can the Party Turn Perrin Here?
entries: They can shake him.
They can make him doubt Tyren.
They can affect how he behaves later.
Do not let one Persuasion roll erase years of choices and end the campaign.
Likewise, do not declare him immune to persuasion because “the plot needs him evil.”
Record the quality of the confrontation:
{@b Cracked:} Perrin is visibly shaken and begins secretly considering a way out.
{@b Defiant:} Perrin believes the party is too frightened of power to understand what Bellweather needs.
{@b Hostile:} Perrin concludes the party will destroy everything he has built if he does not stop them.
This state affects Chapter 17.

entries.name: Perrin’s Core Refusal
entries: Whatever his emotional state, Perrin does {@b not} surrender the power voluntarily here.
He believes giving it up would abandon Bellweather to the same indecision and weakness he has spent years overcoming.
The corruption arc is now explicit.

entries.name: Completing the Regional Arc
entries: After the Perrin confrontation, let the party choose how to weaken Tyren before returning to the central political conflict.
A third regional success, destruction of the Emmer relay, a major alliance, or another equivalent player-driven achievement is enough to establish that Tyren’s outward network has been damaged.
Unused named locations remain in the world and can be visited later.

entries.name: Milestone
entries: Advance the party to {@b level 15} when they have materially broken Tyren’s regional expansion and gained enough allies, routes, or information to act against the central network.

entries.name: DM Truth: Perrin Decides the Party Is a Threat
entries: After the confrontation, Perrin understands that the party knows too much.
If he is Cracked, he delays and searches for a solution that preserves Bellweather without giving up everything.
If Defiant or Hostile, he moves faster.
In every case, Tyren pushes one conclusion:
The party will break the city unless Perrin removes them from the board.
That leads to Zennar.

data.name: Chapter 16: Zennar Outpost
entries: {@b Recommended level:} 15 {@b Expected milestone:} 16 {@b Likely table time:} 1–2 sessions

rows: Make Perrin’s corruption undeniable: he uses civic authority to remove the people threatening his control.
Detect the betrayal, survive or overturn the trap, preserve evidence, return to Bellweather.
Inspect the packet, approach covertly, negotiate with the outpost, fake compliance, escape, expose the order, or fight a limited strike force.
Evidence exists in multiple forms. Capture becomes an escape/social sequence, not campaign-ending helplessness.
Perrin is now using institutions and coercive power to protect his own position, not merely Bellweather.

entries: Run Zennar as a political trap and survival chapter, not a fortress-clearing dungeon.  {@b Quiet kill team:} 1 {@b Assassin}, 2 {@b Veterans}, 1 {@creature Mage|XMM}, and 4 {@b Guards}. Use the Assassin only if the party reaches level 15 well equipped and rested; otherwise replace it with another Veteran.  Attackers withdraw if the operation becomes public, loud, or clearly unsuccessful. Most of the outpost is not aware of the murder order.  The strongest victory is evidence plus escape, not killing the entire garrison.

entries.name: Rewards and Treasure
entries: Evidence is the main reward. If the party resolves the outpost diplomatically, use 1,000 gp-equivalent restitution, supplies, or a civic/diplomatic favor rather than a dungeon hoard.

entries.name: Why Perrin Sends Them
entries: By level 15 the party has:

items: identified Tyren as an ancient emerald dragon;
learned the Radiant Cage exists;
confronted Perrin about the bargain;
damaged Tyren’s regional expansion;
become the people most capable of exposing Perrin and stopping the Well from being reversed.

entries: Perrin now believes the party threatens everything he has built.
Tyren does not need to dominate Perrin into betraying them.
Perrin makes the choice.

entries.name: The Official Mission
entries: Perrin presents an urgent diplomatic/security assignment to {@b Zennar Outpost}.
The visible mission is plausible: establish whether the outpost will cooperate against regional instability and whether it can help isolate Varen Keep.
The party receives sealed credentials and instructions.
The packet contains a second order for the Zennar commandant.

entries.name: Perrin’s Betrayal by State
entries: Use the Perrin state recorded after the party confronted him.

{@b Cracked Perrin:} the hidden order demands detention, disarmament, and removal from Bellweather’s affairs. It authorizes lethal force if the party resists. Perrin tells himself he is preventing a civil conflict, not ordering murder.
{@b Defiant Perrin:} the order describes the party as compromised by Tyren research and authorizes permanent removal if capture is impractical.
{@b Hostile Perrin:} the order is explicitly lethal and asks for proof of death.
All three versions are betrayals.
Do not let Cracked Perrin become innocent because his wording is softer.

entries.name: 1. The Road to Zennar
entries: Give the party one quiet opportunity to inspect the packet before arrival.
Opening and resealing it should be possible with appropriate magic, tools, or care. If they refuse to tamper with diplomatic papers, do not punish them by making the betrayal undetectable later.

entries.name: 2. Approach
entries: Zennar is a disciplined frontier outpost, not a dungeon full of enemies waiting for initiative.
A patrol escorts diplomatic visitors to a controlled reception area.
The soldiers are professional and do not all know about the hidden order.

entries.name: 3. Warning Signs
entries: If the party has not opened the packet, give redundant clues:

items: quarters chosen for containment rather than comfort;
unusual interest in where the party stores weapons;
civilians moved out of their corridor;
a second courier arriving from Bellweather with updated instructions;
guards who appear confused about whether the party is guest or prisoner.

entries: Successful Insight or Investigation reveals the danger earlier. Failure never erases it.

entries.name: 4. The Commandant’s Choice
entries: The commandant is not part of the recurring cast. Use a {@creature Knight|XMM} or {@creature Veteran|XMM} as needed.
The commandant may dislike Perrin’s instruction but still consider it legally valid.
The party can:

items: expose contradictions in the order;
present evidence of Tyren;
convince the commandant Perrin is compromised;
steal the outpost’s copy;
bargain for release;
fake compliance;
escape.

entries: A strong social solution should be as valid as combat.

entries.name: 5. Assassination or Arrest Attempt
entries: If the betrayal reaches violence, use a compact strike force.
Suggested hard encounter for four level-15 PCs:

items: 3 {@b Veterans};
1 {@creature Mage|XMM};
4 {@b Guards} as support and pressure.

entries: If the party is extremely optimized and fully rested, upgrade one Veteran to a {@creature Knight|XMM} or equivalent. Do not turn the entire outpost into one combat encounter.
Attackers withdraw or surrender when the operation becomes publicly indefensible.

entries.name: 6. Evidence
entries: The party can secure up to four forms of proof:

items: the original hidden order;
the commandant’s received copy;
testimony from personnel who were briefed on the operation;
a Bellweather courier record showing the order originated through Perrin’s office.

entries: Two credible forms are enough to make denial politically difficult.

entries.name: Return to Bellweather
entries: The city they return to should feel {@b better and worse at the same time}.
Crime is down.
Major streets are orderly.
Construction and trade are moving quickly.
Public disputes end unusually fast.
People praise Perrin for stabilizing the city while the party was away.
And something is wrong.

Groups of citizens repeat the same phrases. Workers change plans simultaneously. Clerks approve requests they had rejected minutes earlier. People who later come out of the effect cannot explain why a decision felt so obviously correct.
Bellweather is becoming Tyren’s successful prototype.

entries.name: Default Council Positions on Return
entries: Adjust these according to actual play, but use them as a baseline if nothing else has changed.

{@b Wern Ursen} has been removed from direct command or politically sidelined after refusing to place the entire guard structure under Perrin’s unified emergency authority. Perrin uses Wern’s genuinely harsh earlier policies to make the removal look reasonable.

{@b Ulric Evern} remains institutionally active but has unexplained gaps in memory and has signed several decrees he does not remember drafting. Tyren can control Ulric because Ulric is not anchored like Brann or Brakkus. Ulric becomes powerful evidence that something supernatural is happening inside government.

{@b Bishop Brann} publicly refuses to endorse permanent emergency control. He cannot be mentally seized, so Perrin has to isolate, discredit, or politically work around him rather than simply switch him off.

{@creature Brakkus Ledgerhelm|NCFASOC} keeps Ledger House functioning as a refuge. He is not leading an armed rebellion. He simply refuses to hand guests over without lawful cause and cannot be compelled to change his mind supernaturally.

entries.name: No Cause for Alarm Beat
entries: Notices appear throughout Bellweather:

{@b CIVIC NOTICE:} Bellweather remains secure. Essential services are operating at record capacity. Reports of widespread coercion and administrative irregularity are being investigated. Residents are asked to avoid rumor and disruption. {@b There is no cause for alarm.}
At this point the phrase should be frightening precisely because much of the city really does look calm.

entries.name: Perrin’s Point of No Return
entries: The Zennar order matters because Perrin is no longer using control only to solve civic problems.
He used the city’s institutions to protect {@b his own power} from people who could expose him.
Whatever good he still wants for Bellweather, the distinction between the city’s needs and Perrin’s needs has collapsed.

entries.name: Preparing for Varen
entries: The party can return openly, gather Brann/Brakkus/Ulric/Wern as allies, use regional contacts, or move covertly.
Allies should reduce complications rather than join the dragon fight as DM-controlled heroes.
Examples:

items: Brakkus keeps controlled civilians and guards from overwhelming the party’s escape route;
Brann protects noncombatants and helps break a citywide influence pulse;
Wern provides routes, timing, and military intelligence;
Ulric exposes legal orders and removes bureaucratic barriers;
regional allies cut off reinforcements or supply routes.

entries.name: Milestone
entries: Advance the party to {@b level 16} when the Zennar betrayal is survived, credible evidence is preserved, and the party is ready to move against the Radiant Well.

data.name: Chapter 17: Varen Keep and the Radiant Cage

entries.name: Maps
entries: {@link Player Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/player/varen_keep.webp}
{@link DM Keyed Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/dm/varen_keep.webp}
{@b Recommended level:} 16 {@b Campaign finale} {@b Likely table time:} 2–3 sessions

entries.name: Modern Running Sheet

rows: Stop Tyren’s attempt to reverse the Radiant Cage, confront Perrin’s choices, release and defeat the dragon, and decide Bellweather’s political and magical future.
Reach the lower keep, disable the outward-control network, stop the Well reversal, survive Tyren’s release, defeat the ancient emerald dragon.
Infiltration, coalition assault, secret routes, sabotage, negotiation with controlled defenders, or direct attack. Perrin’s final stance depends on earlier play.
Missing objectives makes the dragon fight harder; it never removes the dragon payoff or ends the campaign through one failed check.
The “Spirit of the City” is physically real, physically imprisoned, and has used Perrin as the door through which an old conquest could begin again.

entries: {@i Use the existing Varen Keep map. Run it as set pieces rather than a room-by-room clear.}

The final payoff is a {@b guaranteed dragon fight}. Earlier success changes Tyren's advantages; it does not remove the dragon from the campaign.  {@b Stage 1 — Reach the lower keep:} 2–3 set pieces using {@creature Veteran|XMM}, {@creature Knight|XMM}, {@creature Mage|XMM}, {@creature Helmed Horror|XMM}, or controlled defenders appropriate to the allies and nodes still active.  {@b Stage 2 — Break the nodes:} objective encounters, not room-by-room clearing.  {@b Stage 3 — Perrin at the Well:} social/ritual confrontation with Perrin's state determined by earlier choices.  {@b Stage 4 — Tyren released:} use the official {@creature Ancient Emerald Dragon|FTD} stat block as the chassis, plus the Tyren overlay in the Custom Game Statistics appendix.  Do not add a second dragon. Soren is not part of this version's central finale.

entries.name: Rewards and Treasure
entries: By level 16, strong items are appropriate. Across Varen Keep, award at most {@b one major permanent item per character} if the party's existing gear supports it. The Radiant Well is a story object, not portable treasure.

entries.name: The Situation
entries: Tyren and Perrin are attempting to reverse the Radiant Well.

Perrin believes fully opening the Well will give him enough power to end Bellweather’s instability permanently. He now sees direct control as an efficient form of governance: crime can be stopped before it begins, corrupt officials can be made to act properly, and civic projects can proceed without obstruction.
Tyren wants something much larger.

The same reversed current that would let Perrin dominate Bellweather will let Tyren push his mind outward through every connected person, relay, trade route, and controlled node the network has established.
Bellweather is the first city.
Tyren intends it to be the first of many.

entries.name: Why the Dragon Fight Is Guaranteed
entries: The party cannot solve the campaign by simply leaving Tyren sealed while breaking a few political connections.
The Radiant Cage and outward-control network have become entangled.
To stop Tyren from broadcasting through the Well, the party must disable the mechanisms reversing the current.
Doing so forces Tyren’s dispersed psychic presence back toward his physical body—the same principle used by the Unturned fifty years ago.
But fifty years of strain, Perrin’s willing conduit, and the reversed Well have damaged the original prison beyond repair.
When the party successfully stops the outward broadcast, the {@b Radiant Cage fails physically}.
Tyren is released.
Stopping the mind-control apocalypse causes the final dragon fight.
That is the price of ending the threat instead of postponing it.

entries.name: Finale Structure
entries: Run Varen Keep as four major stages.

entries.name: Stage 1 — Reach the Lower Keep
entries: Use 2–3 set pieces, not thirty rooms.
Existing map elements can include:

items: outer watchposts;
the thorn maze;
barracks and controlled defenders;
unstable teleporters;
officer quarters;
service tunnels discovered through earlier maps or allies.

entries.name: Defenders
entries: Most defenders are not fanatics. Some are controlled guards, workers, criminals, or mercenaries.
Use {@b Veterans}, {@b Knights}, {@b Guards}, {@b Mages}, and other appropriate official stat blocks in small groups.
Characters who use mind wards, {@i Dispel Magic}, {@i Greater Restoration} after severing a connection, or nonlethal tactics can free or bypass some defenders.
Do not require the party to slaughter Bellweather citizens under supernatural control.

entries.name: Ally Benefits
entries: For each major ally or regional success earned before the finale, remove one complication:

items: no exterior reinforcement wave;
one watchpost already neutralized;
a service route is open;
controlled civilians have been evacuated;
one defensive ward is already disabled.

entries: Do not add allied NPCs to the main dragon initiative unless the players explicitly engineer that outcome.

entries.name: Stage 2 — Break the Three Nodes
entries: The Radiant Cage complex contains three systems that Tyren and Perrin are using to reverse the original ritual.
The party can tackle them in any order.

entries.name: Node A: The Chorus Chamber
entries: This chamber maintains Tyren’s active connection to controlled minds outside the Keep.
It contains resonant emerald material similar to the device at Emmer Hold.
{@b Objective:} destroy, disrupt, or ward the resonance array.
Possible methods:

items: physical destruction;
Arcana or Religion challenge while under attack;
using the Rellan ritual component;
overloading the array with psychic/radiant energy;
a creative equivalent.

entries: {@b Benefit if disabled:}

items: controlled reinforcements outside the Keep lose coordination;
Tyren cannot use the campaign-specific {@b Seize the Anchored} effect during the dragon fight;
when Tyren dies, he has no prepared network into which his consciousness can easily escape.

entries: This is the most important node for a clean victory.

entries.name: Node B: The Civic Relay
entries: Perrin has built an administrative-magical network around the Well: orders, signal crystals, schedules, city maps, and lists of officials and institutions.
This is the machinery of Bellweather being treated like one body.
{@b Objective:} sever Perrin’s ability to direct the network.
Possible methods:

items: destroy the central relay;
replace the command sequence with a shutdown order;
use Ulric’s official seals to invalidate linked civic instructions;
use Wern’s military codes to break guard synchronization;
persuade Perrin to deactivate it.

entries: {@b Benefit if disabled:}

items: no controlled guard/minion support during the final fight;
Bellweather begins waking up before Tyren is dead;
Perrin loses the immediate proof that “control works.”

entries.name: Node C: The Well Reversal
entries: This mechanism is physically reversing the Radiant Well’s original inward pull.
{@b Objective:} stop the outward flow.
Possible methods:

items: stabilize and reverse arcane regulators;
break the control lattice;
complete part of the old Unturned rite;
force the system into shutdown.

entries: {@b Benefit if disabled:}

items: Tyren cannot project his will citywide during the final confrontation;
the global-scale plan ends;
the process of shutting it down begins the unavoidable physical collapse of the Radiant Cage.

entries.name: Running the Nodes
entries: Each node should be an objective encounter with defenders and environmental pressure rather than a single Arcana roll.
A good default is {@b 3 successes before 2 complications} using different plausible actions while a small elite force interferes.
Do not require one specific skill.

entries.name: Stage 3 — Perrin at the Well
entries: Perrin is present in the lower complex when the final node is threatened.
This is not a mandatory boss fight against Perrin.
His behavior depends on the state recorded during the level-14 confrontation and what the party has done since.

entries.name: Cracked Perrin
entries: Perrin has been trying not to admit that the party was right.
Seeing the physical containment machinery and the Well destabilizing can finally break the story he has told himself about the Spirit.
He may help disable one node, order controlled defenders to stand down, or give the party a crucial piece of access.
He still remains responsible for everything he chose before this moment.

entries.name: Defiant Perrin
entries: Perrin believes the party is about to destroy the only power capable of permanently fixing Bellweather.
He tries to stop them through guards, locks, civic authority, and the relay system.
He may still hesitate when Tyren begins speaking openly about control beyond Bellweather.

entries.name: Hostile Perrin
entries: Perrin has fused his own political survival with Bellweather’s future.
He actively attempts to keep the Well reversal running and treats the party as enemies of the city.
Use an appropriate non-boss NPC chassis if Perrin must enter combat, but keep his real power in command, access, and controlled defenders rather than suddenly turning him into a high-level wizard.

entries.name: The Truth Perrin Cannot Rationalize
entries: As the final node fails, Tyren no longer needs to maintain the fiction of being Bellweather’s benevolent spirit.
Perrin experiences the dragon’s full presence for the first time.
The party should not need a speech to understand what happened.
The chamber shakes.
Emerald light moves beneath the stone.
The enormous restraints below begin to break.
Whatever Perrin thought he made a bargain with, it has claws, wings, and a body large enough to have required a fortress to bury.
Perrin’s reaction belongs to the campaign state:

items: horror;
denial;
rage at Tyren;
desperate insistence that the party can still control the situation;
or a final attempt to help.

entries: Do not use Tyren’s deception to erase Perrin’s agency. Perrin was deceived about what Tyren was, but Perrin knowingly chose manipulation, criminal conspiracy, direct control, and betrayal.

entries.name: The Release
entries: When the Well Reversal is stopped, the Radiant Cage performs one final version of its original purpose: it yanks Tyren’s projected consciousness back toward his own body.
The damaged prison cannot survive the return.
The lower chamber opens.
Tyren is released.
This is the campaign’s dragon payoff.

entries.name: Stage 4 — Tyren, Ancient Emerald Dragon
entries: Use the official {@creature Ancient Emerald Dragon|FTD} stat block from {@i Fizban’s Treasury of Dragons} as Tyren’s base statistics.
Do {@b not} weaken the core dragon stat block merely because the party is level 16. This is the final fight of a level-3-to-16 campaign and should demand major resources.
Balance the encounter through the objectives the party completed, not by quietly reducing Tyren’s identity.

entries.name: Default Final Fight
entries: If the party disabled {@b two or more nodes}, fight Tyren as the full official Ancient Emerald Dragon without an additional minion wave.
Use Varen’s lower chamber and Well as meaningful terrain.
Allow the party the benefit of every defensive preparation they earned.

entries.name: If the Chorus Chamber Still Functions
entries: Tyren retains a campaign-specific legendary/lair option:

entries.name: Seize the Anchored
entries: Tyren targets one anchored PC or Jord he can perceive. The target makes the appropriate Wisdom save.
On a failure, Tyren imposes one Command-like imperative on the target’s next turn, following the campaign’s hard ceiling:

items: one compelled turn/action only;
no forced attack on an ally;
no expenditure of a major limited resource;
no irreversible roleplay decision;
no suicidal order.

entries: A {@item Ring of Mind Shielding} makes the wearer immune.
Brakkus and Bishop Brann are immune if they are somehow present.
If the Chorus Chamber was disabled, Tyren {@b cannot use this ability}.

entries.name: If the Civic Relay Still Functions
entries: Add one limited support complication rather than a full army:

items: 2 controlled {@b Veterans} arrive at the start of round 2; or
one controlled {@creature Mage|XMM} supports from a balcony until freed/defeated; or
a civic defense mechanism creates cover/hazard for Tyren.

entries: Do not stack all three.
If the Civic Relay was disabled, Tyren fights without controlled Bellweather support.

entries.name: If the Well Reversal Was Only Partially Stabilized
entries: Use one additional environmental effect at initiative count 20:

items: psychic shockwave causing forced movement;
radiant eruption from a marked zone;
temporary difficult terrain as gravity/force bends toward the Well.

entries: A completely stabilized Well removes this extra effect.

entries.name: Tyren’s Tactics
entries: Tyren has spent fifty years thinking about control.
He should fight intelligently.
He uses mobility, psychic abilities, breath weapon, terrain, and isolation rather than standing in melee until dead.
He recognizes the Ring of Mind Shielding as a threat if its immunity becomes obvious.
He understands Brakkus and Brann are the same kind of problem the Unturned were.
He does not waste turns repeatedly attempting effects on creatures he knows are immune.

entries.name: No Forced PvP
entries: Even in the final fight, Tyren’s anchored-mind control does not force a PC to attack another PC.
Keep the premise consistent all the way to the end.

entries.name: Tyren at 0 Hit Points
entries: The campaign established that killing a host was not automatically enough to kill Tyren.
The final objectives determine whether that remains a problem.

entries.name: If the Chorus Chamber Was Disabled
entries: Tyren’s external network has collapsed.
When his physical body dies, there is no prepared web of dominated minds for his consciousness to inhabit.
The Radiant Well pulls the remaining psychic presence inward and it dies with the dragon.
The threat ends.

entries.name: If the Chorus Chamber Still Functions
entries: Tyren attempts to escape through the remaining network.
Run a short final objective challenge: {@b 4 successes before 3 complications}.
Valid actions include:

items: destroying the Chorus system now;
using the Radiant Well to pull the escaping mind inward;
using the Ring of Mind Shielding as a protected contact point while manipulating the network;
Arcana or Religion to complete the old containment sequence;
{@i Dispel Magic}, {@i Greater Restoration}, or another relevant high-level spell used creatively;
severing controlled NPCs from the relay;
another plausible player plan.

entries: Failure should create a costly complication, not erase the campaign victory outright. Tyren may leave behind a fragment, scar, or future threat, but he does not simply possess a PC and declare the campaign lost.

entries.name: Perrin After Tyren
entries: Separating or killing Tyren does not automatically absolve Perrin.
The relevant facts remain:

items: Perrin willingly accepted supernatural influence;
he used it to manipulate people;
he organized criminals to discredit the Council;
he concealed Tyren’s independent control after discovering it;
he knowingly chose direct mental control at Storen Gate;
he continued after learning Tyren was the same force that nearly destroyed old Bellweather;
he used civic authority against the party at Zennar;
he attempted to make control permanent.

entries: Perrin was deceived about Tyren’s identity.
Perrin was also corrupted through his own choices.
Let the players and surviving Bellweather institutions decide what happens next.
Possible outcomes include trial, imprisonment, exile, political collapse, cooperation in repairing the damage, or another consequence earned through play.
Do not script a redemption and do not script an execution.

entries.name: The Radiant Well
entries: After Tyren is defeated, the Well remains.
The party and Bellweather must decide what to do with a source of power capable of both containment and mass psychic amplification.
Possible choices include:

items: seal access;
destroy the control infrastructure while preserving the natural/magical Well;
place it under shared custody among multiple institutions;
study it under strict safeguards;
collapse Varen’s lower chamber;
another player-created solution.

entries: No single Council member automatically gets control.
Brakkus’s only strong position is that no one person should quietly control something capable of taking away another person’s will.
Brann emphasizes consent and the moral danger of “good” coercion.
Ulric wants transparent legal custody and records.
Wern wants to know how the city defends the site from whoever comes next.

entries.name: Epilogue: No Cause for Alarm
entries: Do not end with a generic parade unless the table wants one.
Show concrete consequences:

items: people waking from control and learning what they did;
businesses deciding whether Perrin-era agreements still stand;
guards confronting orders they carried out under influence;
families returning to normal routines;
political arguments happening openly again;
Ledger House full of people disagreeing loudly because they are finally allowed to.

entries: The hopeful ending is not that Bellweather becomes calm.
It is that Bellweather becomes capable of tolerating disagreement without treating disagreement as failure.
If the title gets one final spoken callback, earn it from the actual ending.
A surviving official might begin another reassuring notice and stop before writing the familiar phrase.
Brakkus might be asked whether the city is safe now and answer with something dry rather than certainty.
Do not force the words.
The campaign has already taught the table what they mean.

data.name: Appendix A: Campaign Control Sheet
entries: Use this page between sessions. It is the simplest possible version of the campaign behind the screen.

entries.name: The Truth
entries: {@b Perrin wanted enough influence to restore the Cardon fortune and make Bellweather vibrant again.}
{@b Tyren offered that power while pretending to be the Spirit of the City.}
{@b Perrin organized criminals to discredit the Council.}
{@b Tyren used the connected criminal network to experiment with mass mind control.}
{@b Perrin discovered this and kept the bargain.}
{@b Perrin eventually decided direct control worked better than influence.}
{@b Tyren is an ancient emerald dragon trapped in the Radiant Cage beneath Varen Keep.}
{@b Tyren wants complete control of every mind in the world.}
{@b Bellweather is his prototype.}

entries.name: Perrin Corruption Track
