entries: Do not advance this because a certain number of sessions passed. Advance it when the corresponding story choice happens.

rows: “I can help people choose what is good for Bellweather.”
“The Council is the obstacle. I can create the crisis that proves it.”
“I did not order what the Spirit did, but exposing it would destroy everything.”
“The results are good. Maybe the old records misunderstood.”
“The Spirit can control people, but that power can still be used responsibly.”
“Not using the power when it can save lives would be irresponsible.”
“People should not be allowed to obstruct what Bellweather needs.”
“The party threatens the city because it threatens my ability to lead it.”
“A perfectly ordered Bellweather is worth the cost.”
Dreams and light influence through Perrin
Perrin can nudge individual ordinary NPCs
Tyren uses the criminal communication structure
Tyren coordinates groups and begins Mass Suggestion-style effects
Brief Command-style pressure reaches anchored PCs/Jord; stronger control reaches ordinary NPCs
Tyren can directly control ordinary people for sustained periods
Tyren attempts citywide/worldward broadcast through the Radiant Well

data.name: Appendix B: Tyren Control Quick Rules

entries.name: Ordinary NPC — Early
entries: Use {@i {@spell suggestion}} as the rules model.

items: Wisdom save.
Charmed on failure.
Instruction must be achievable.
No obviously self-destructive command.
Damage or appropriate magic can end the effect as normal for the model.

entries.name: Ordinary NPC — Group
entries: Use {@i {@spell mass suggestion}} as the rules model.
Use this when a scene requires a coordinated group, not as a casual background power.

entries.name: Ordinary NPC — Late Direct Control
entries: Use {@i {@spell dominate person}} as the rules model.
This is for late-campaign ordinary NPCs only.
Do not use Dominate Person-style control on the PCs or Jord.

entries.name: PCs and Jord
entries: Use the campaign’s {@b Command ceiling}.

items: Wisdom saving throw.
One turn / one compelled action on failure.
Full control returns immediately.
No forced attacks on allies.
No forced major resource expenditure.
No irreversible roleplay choices.
No suicidal commands.

entries.name: Brakkus and Bishop Brann
entries: Direct Tyren control fails.
No save is needed when the only effect is Tyren attempting to seize their actions.
They remain vulnerable to ordinary persuasion, deception, threats, environmental danger, and unrelated magic.

entries.name: Ring of Mind Shielding
entries: A wearer is immune to Tyren’s control because the ring prevents the unwanted telepathic connection Tyren needs to establish.
This is a campaign-specific interaction with Tyren, not a blanket rewrite of the item.

data.name: Appendix C: Clue Ladder
entries: The mystery should remain solvable even when players miss individual details.

entries.name: Phase 1 — Coordination
entries: The party should learn:

items: separate gangs use the same signals;
Iron Covenant logistics connect them;
some orders appear without a recognized issuer.

entries: Sources:

items: Kellan schedules;
Koven ledgers;
captured criminals;
the coded Blackstone ledger already held by the Council.

entries.name: Phase 2 — Historical Pattern
entries: The party should learn:

items: Old Bellweather experienced the same impossible coordination;
the name Tyren appears in sealed records;
a few people called the Unturned resisted.

entries: Sources:

items: Savin diary;
command-stone report;
old civic circular.

entries.name: Phase 3 — Possession
entries: The party should learn:

items: Tyren can occupy living hosts;
destroying a host is not necessarily enough;
the Radiant Cage forced Tyren back into his own body;
resistance seems connected to certainty of self.

entries: Sources:

items: Marren Library;
Brann/Brakkus behavior;
Paden event.

entries.name: Phase 4 — Physical Truth
entries: The party should learn:

items: Tyren is an ancient emerald dragon;
Tyren is physically alive beneath Varen Keep;
the Radiant Well powers the prison;
reversing the Well would project his mind outward.

entries: Sources:

items: Maren Isle missing volume;
Rellan oral history;
Varen machinery.

entries.name: Phase 5 — Perrin
entries: The party should be able to infer:

items: Cardon-linked money helped build the criminal network;
Perrin benefited from the crises;
Tyren needs a willing conduit;
synchronized expansion originates in Bellweather;
Perrin’s rise tracks the network’s growth.

entries: No single clue should read “Perrin did it.”
The intended reveal is a confrontation with a person the party has come to know, not finding a signed villain confession in a drawer.

data.name: Appendix D: Pepper Continuity and Payoffs

entries.name: Legal Consequence
entries: Pepper’s sentence is already established and must not expand because the campaign changed.

items: Five mandatory Council missions total.
Kellan’s Well is Mission 1 and unpaid for Pepper.
Missions 2–5 are paid normally.
Refusal or abandonment means jail.
House arrest at Ledger House remains until completion.
Leaving with Brakkus or on Council business is permitted.

entries: Recommended mission count in this campaign:
Do not silently add more compulsory jobs.

entries.name: Lessa Dorn and Kav Orin
entries: Lessa and Kav remain recurring supporting NPCs through the five missions because they are known Council surveyors and were part of the chain that reported Jarrock’s accusation.
Their purpose is not to prosecute Pepper repeatedly.
Use them as:

items: map/route specialists;
field documentation witnesses;
familiar Council faces;
people whose opinion can evolve according to Pepper’s actual conduct.

entries: At Mission 5 completion they can be present when the Council closes the field obligation.

entries.name: Caleb’s Family
entries: The family story is separate from the sentence.
{@b Kerrik:} aarakocra, Caleb’s best friend, brings the news.
{@b Mara:} human, Caleb’s widow.
{@b Elise:} human, Caleb’s daughter.
Mara’s request for Pepper to help Elise is not leverage, payment, or a legal requirement.
Elise’s psychic affliction is collateral damage from Tyren’s network and can be removed by {@b Greater Restoration} or equivalent high magic after the psychic connection is broken.
Pepper may help or refuse. Preserve that choice.

rows: asks numbers, routes, defenses, failure points
tightens security and chain of command
Warm older dwarf in mail and robes
asks who is hurt and who pays the cost
becomes morally direct and very still
reframes problems as solvable civic projects
protects people first and speaks less

entries.name: Ulric Evern — Procedure
entries: Ulric’s strength is institutional memory.
He believes power should be recorded, limited, funded, and reviewable.
Perrin increasingly sees him as a person who can always explain why the right thing cannot happen quickly.
Late campaign, Ulric is vulnerable to Tyren’s direct control. Memory gaps and inexplicable signatures can become evidence of supernatural interference.
Ulric is not secretly corrupt unless actual play makes him so.

entries.name: Wern Ursen — Security
entries: Wern responds to growing danger with stronger security.
He should sometimes be right.
He should sometimes go too far.
Use checkpoints, curfews, aggressive patrol proposals, and rigid chains of command to make him a credible political opponent and plausible suspect without making him the hidden villain.
Perrin benefits from Wern looking authoritarian.

entries.name: Bishop Brann — Limits
entries: Brann keeps asking who pays the cost of “necessary” power.
His immunity means Perrin cannot solve Brann by controlling him.
As Perrin rises, Brann becomes more dangerous politically because he remains capable of sincere dissent when other people begin falling into supernatural agreement.

entries.name: Perrin Cardon — Results

data.name: Appendix H: Treasure and Magic Policy
entries: Continue the current campaign’s curated treasure philosophy.

entries.name: Levels 4–8

items: useful consumables;

story-relevant property, documents, and favors;

data.name: Appendix I: Session Prep Template for This Version
entries: This campaign is designed so the DM does not need to write an entire session from scratch every week.
For each session, prepare only the following.

entries.name: 1. What Can Change Tonight?
entries: One sentence.
Examples:

items: The party can prove Koven House is the Covenant hub.
The party can learn Tyren controlled Old Bellweather.
Perrin can cross the line into direct control.

entries.name: 2. Three Scenes
entries: {@b Arrival/choice.} Present the problem and at least two approaches.
{@b Pressure.} Combat, investigation, social conflict, hazard, or time pressure complicates the plan.
{@b Decision.} End around a choice, objective, or confrontation that changes the situation.

entries.name: 3. Essential Information
entries: Write the clues the party must be able to obtain.
Never attach a campaign-critical clue to one pass/fail roll.

entries.name: 4. Opposition
entries: For each active group, write:

items: what it wants;
what it is doing now;
what makes it retreat, surrender, bargain, or change plans.

entries.name: 5. Perrin/Tyren Movement
entries: Ask one question:
{@b Did anything happen tonight that should change Perrin’s corruption or Tyren’s reach?}
If no, do not force one.
Not every session needs a main-plot reveal.

entries.name: 6. Return to Ledger House
entries: Prepare:

items: one visible city change;
one familiar face;
one consequence;
one live opportunity.

entries: That is enough.

data.name: Appendix J: DM Guardrails
entries: These rules protect the campaign from becoming more complicated than the story requires.

items: {@b Do not make every antagonist part of Tyren’s conspiracy.}
{@b Do not make Bishop Brann secretly evil.}
{@b Do not make Wern secretly evil just because his security policies are harsh.}
{@b Do not retroactively make the Slums or Blackstone secret Perrin plans.}
{@b Do not exceed the Command ceiling on PCs or Jord.}
{@b Do not take player roleplay decisions away through mind control.}
{@b Do not make the Iron Covenant a Tyren-worshiping cult.} They are criminals Perrin helped organize; Tyren hijacks their network.
{@b Do not turn trauma itself into a magical superpower.} Resistance comes from an anchored sense of self; trauma is only one path by which that identity formed.
{@b Do not absolve Perrin because Tyren lied about being the Spirit of the City.} Perrin’s later choices remain his.
{@b Do not remove the dragon fight.} The campaign culminates with Tyren physically released and fought as an ancient emerald dragon.
{@b Do not shorten the campaign below level 16.} The players were promised that progression.
{@b Do not let chapter order become another reclamation checklist.} Use the story hooks and player choices to move between the named places.

data.name: Appendix L: Custom Game Statistics and Overlays
entries: These entries modify or wrap official stat blocks already available in 5etools. They intentionally avoid recreating published monster text.

entries.name: Tyren — Ancient Emerald Dragon Overlay
entries: {@b Base stat block:} {@creature Ancient Emerald Dragon|FTD}.
Use the official block unchanged except for the campaign-specific additions below.

entries.name: Anchored Mind Rule
entries: Tyren's ordinary control effects cannot hold an anchored mind.

items: {@b Brakkus Ledgerhelm and Bishop Brann:} immune to Tyren's direct supernatural influence and control.

{@b Player characters and Jord:} resistant. If Tyren attempts direct control, call for the appropriate Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, Tyren may compel {@b one single action} modeled on {@spell command}. Control ends immediately after that action.
{@b Ring of Mind Shielding:} the wearer is immune to Tyren's influence and control because the ring blocks the telepathic connection Tyren requires.
This rule never allows Tyren to force a PC or Jord into multi-round control, forced roleplay, permanent belief changes, or ongoing domination.

entries.name: Voice Through the Chorus
entries: When a Radiant Cage node or psychic relay is active, Tyren can issue a telepathic imperative to creatures connected to his network.
For {@b ordinary NPCs}, model the effect with the closest appropriate official spell for the story stage: {@spell suggestion}, {@spell mass suggestion}, {@spell geas}, or {@spell dominate person}.
For {@b anchored minds}, the effect collapses to the one-action {@spell command}-style ceiling above.

entries.name: Seize the Anchored
entries: When the finale needs direct pressure, Tyren may target one anchored creature he can perceive within the range you are already using for the official dragon's psychic abilities.
The target makes a Wisdom saving throw against Tyren's normal save DC.

On a failure, choose one simple imperative such as {@b Approach, Drop, Flee, Grovel, Halt, Move, Release, or Protect}. On that creature's next turn, the imperative consumes no more than one action or equivalent brief compelled behavior. Control then ends.

Do not use this to force direct attacks on another PC unless the player explicitly enjoys that kind of scene. The default is movement, dropping/handing over an object, opening/closing something, standing aside, or losing one action.

entries.name: Node Advantages
entries: Each active node in Varen Keep grants Tyren one campaign advantage.
{@b Chorus Chamber active:} once per round, Tyren can use Seize the Anchored without spending a legendary-action equivalent. Ordinary dominated defenders also remain coordinated.
{@b Civic Relay active:} controlled defenders gain advantage on their first saving throw each round and can reposition as a coordinated reaction when Tyren moves.
{@b Well Reversal active:} one lair/environmental effect tied to the Radiant Well remains available each round.
Disable a node and remove its advantage immediately.

entries.name: Normal Perrin
entries: Use {@creature Noble|XMM} as the baseline if statistics are needed. Perrin is not designed as a frontline combat encounter.

entries.name: Borrowed Influence
entries: While Tyren's connection is subtle, Perrin can create an effect modeled on {@spell suggestion} against an ordinary NPC who can perceive him. Use a Wisdom save appropriate to the current tier; DC 14–16 is sufficient early.
This is supernatural influence, not ordinary Persuasion.

entries.name: Mass Influence
entries: Late in the campaign, when Tyren is actively channeling through Perrin, model Perrin's influence over ordinary crowds using {@spell mass suggestion}.
Do not use Mass Influence on PCs, Jord, Brakkus, or Bishop Brann.

entries.name: Borrowed Command
entries: When Tyren is actively present, Perrin can serve as the point of origin for Tyren's one-action effect against an anchored mind.
This follows the {@b Anchored Mind Rule} exactly. Perrin never gets a stronger control effect over a PC or Jord.

entries.name: Combat Use
entries: If Perrin becomes physically hostile, he should rely on guards, positioning, social leverage, and Tyren's borrowed abilities. Do not inflate him into a high-CR martial boss merely to make the scene harder.

entries.name: Brakkus Ledgerhelm
entries: Use the existing authoritative {@creature Brakkus Ledgerhelm|NCFASOC} custom stat block from {@i No Cause for Alarm: Ruins of Bellweather}.
For this campaign add:

{@b Anchored Immunity.} Tyren cannot magically influence, charm, command, dominate, possess, or otherwise take direct control of Brakkus. This is the combined result of Brakkus's divine aura/protection and a deeply anchored identity shaped by trauma. It does not make Brakkus immune to lies, ordinary Persuasion, political pressure, or emotional manipulation.

entries.name: Bishop Brann
entries: {@b Base stat block:} {@creature Priest|XMM} unless a stronger priestly block is clearly needed for a late-tier defensive scene.
{@b Anchored Immunity.} Tyren cannot magically influence, charm, command, dominate, possess, or otherwise take direct control of Brann.

Brann's anchor is his devotion reinforced by childhood trauma: he watched his sister murdered by a gang and built his adult identity around refusing to let violence, fear, or hatred dictate who he becomes.
Do not tie that gang to the Iron Covenant or Tyren.

entries.name: Jord
entries: {@b Base stat block:} use the established Jord statistics if available; otherwise {@creature Priest|XMM} is sufficient for NPC combat.
{@b Anchored Resistance.} Jord is resistant, not immune. Tyren can never do more than the one-action {@spell command}-style effect on him.

Jord's anchor is intentionally a little funny: he lives for a good deal so completely that some part of his mind interrogates every proposition for the catch. Tyren can force through for a moment; he cannot keep Jord's mind.

entries.name: Wern Ursen
entries: Use {@creature Veteran|XMM} for most scenes or {@creature Knight|XMM} when Wern needs to function as a serious armored commander. Wern is an elf and a career soldier. He is not secretly controlled by Tyren by default.

entries.name: Ulric Evern
entries: Use {@creature Noble|XMM} if statistics are required. Ulric's power is procedural and institutional, not combat-focused.

data.name: Appendix M: Artwork and Map Index
entries: This edition reuses the same NCFA source-plate asset paths as {@i Ruins of Bellweather}.

The Mansion District and Zennar Outpost do not have dedicated source plates in the current NCFA asset index. Run them from their text geography, existing Bellweather geography, and modular encounter areas rather than inventing a fake source map.

data.name: Appendix N: Table-Use Chapter Checklist
entries: Before running any chapter, verify:

items: {@b Level and milestone} match the campaign table.
{@b Map} is visible or the scene is intentionally theater-of-the-mind.
{@b Encounter roster} is distributed across scenes rather than stacked into one initiative.
{@b Stat blocks} are loaded in 5etools before play.
{@b Essential clues} cannot disappear behind one failed roll.
{@b Opposition morale} is defined.
{@b Rewards and Treasure} is prepared.
{@b Perrin/Tyren movement} is known behind the screen.
{@b Pepper continuity} is updated if still relevant.
{@b Return to Ledger House} includes one visible Bellweather change, one consequence, and one live opportunity.

data.name: Final DM Summary
entries: If the campaign ever feels complicated, return to this:

{@b Perrin sincerely wants Bellweather restored. Tyren pretends to be the Spirit of the City and gives him influence. Perrin uses it for good, then for manipulation, then to organize criminals against the Council. Tyren hijacks that criminal network and learns to control groups. Perrin repeatedly discovers the danger and keeps the power because the results work. Eventually he chooses direct control himself. Tyren is actually an ancient emerald dragon trapped beneath Varen Keep, and Bellweather is his experiment for controlling every mind in the world. The party uncovers the truth, breaks the network, stops the Radiant Well from broadcasting Tyren’s will, releases the dragon in the process, and fights him at level 16.}
Everything else is an adventure that happens around that story.

entries: While Brakkus is conscious, he and friendly creatures within 10 feet of him gain a +4 bonus to saving throws.

trait.name: Aura of Courage
entries: While Brakkus is conscious, he and friendly creatures within 10 feet of him can't be {@condition frightened}.

trait.name: Aura of Devotion

trait.name: Lay on Hands (80 HP/Long Rest)
entries: Brakkus has a pool of 80 hit points of healing. As an action, he can touch a creature and restore any number of hit points remaining in the pool. He can instead spend 5 points to cure one disease or neutralize one poison affecting the target.

trait.name: Fire Walker

1/Long Rest: {@spell Shield|XPHB} (from Magic Initiate)

action.name: The Appendix
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 12} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}11 ({@damage 1d8 + 7}) slashing damage plus 2 ({@damage 1d4}) radiant damage.

action.name: Divine Smite
entries: When Brakkus hits a creature with The Appendix, he can expend a spell slot to deal additional radiant damage: 2d8 with a 1st-level slot, 3d8 with a 2nd-level slot, 4d8 with a 3rd-level slot, or 5d8 with a 4th-level slot. The damage increases by 1d8 against a Fiend or Undead, subject to the normal Divine Smite maximum.

action.name: Sacred Flame
entries: One creature Brakkus can see within 60 feet must succeed on a DC 17 Dexterity saving throw or take 13 ({@damage 3d8}) radiant damage. The target gains no benefit from Half Cover or Three-Quarters Cover for this save.

action.name: Word of Radiance
entries: Each creature of Brakkus's choice within 5 feet of him must succeed on a DC 17 Constitution saving throw or take 10 ({@damage 3d6}) radiant damage.

action.name: Sacred Weapon (Channel Divinity; 1/Short or Long Rest)
entries: As an action, Brakkus imbues The Appendix with positive energy for 1 minute. He adds his Charisma modifier (+4) to attack rolls made with the weapon, raising its attack bonus to +16, and the weapon emits bright light in a 20-foot radius and dim light for another 20 feet.

action.name: Turn the Unholy (Channel Divinity; 1/Short or Long Rest)
entries: As an action, Brakkus presents his holy symbol. Each Fiend or Undead within 30 feet that can see or hear him must succeed on a DC 17 Wisdom saving throw or be Turned for 1 minute or until it takes damage.

reaction.name: Shield (1/Long Rest)
entries: When Brakkus is hit by an attack roll or targeted by {@spell Magic Missile|XPHB}, he casts {@spell Shield|XPHB}. Until the start of his next turn, his AC becomes 29, including against the triggering attack, and he takes no damage from Magic Missile.
Brakkus is a roughly forty-eight-year-old half-orc, retired adventurer and mercenary, and level 16 Oath of Devotion paladin of Torm. He owns Ledger House in Bellweather and maintains it as a refuge.
Brakkus is a home-base NPC, not a companion character. His default priorities are protect civilians, stabilize downed allies, contain the threat, then defeat the aggressor.
Challenge Rating. The listed CR is provided for encounter-building purposes; Brakkus is a 16th-level paladin.

item.name: The Appendix
entries: You gain a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic longsword.
On a hit, the weapon deals an extra {@damage 1d4} radiant damage.
The Appendix was given to Brakkus Ledgerhelm by High Justiciar Vance Halford and named in honor of Elena's love of books.
The item does not require attunement.
